text:
alex: heads-up — after pushing the cu12 toolkit images to eu-west pool, ~14 nodes flipped to NotReady and a bunch of containers restarted. low-level errors in kube logs. anyone seen this?

mira: saw a couple of crashloops earlier, looked like linker/runtime mismatch. can you paste the node dmesg / container logs?

alex: pasted the minimal logs to the thread:
```
containerd: failed to start process: error while loading shared libraries: /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2: version `GLIBC_2.34' not found
lld: /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so: undefined symbol: __tls_get_addr
```

jon: @alex that first error smells like distro glibc vs toolkit built against newer glibc. which base image are you using for the cu12 builds?

alex: ubuntu:18.04 base for some of the older jobs. we rebuilt runtime images yesterday to include toolkit12 system libs.

mira: yep that's the problem — cu12 toolkits in our images are linked against glibc >= 2.34. ubuntu18.04 has 2.27. mixing is causing the dynamic loader to choke.

lee: we also observed NCCL transport errors after the rebuild on multi-GPU pods: `ncclCommInitRank failed, unrecognized plugin`. Might be ABI changes between compiler toolchains used to build nccl/driver.

kate: cost note — we triggered a cluster-wide rolling rebuild of images to be cu12-compatible which used ~2.2k GPU-hours across regions. SRE wanted to know whether to continue or rollback.

alex: proposal: tag images with toolkit-major (cu11 vs cu12), avoid in-place overwrite of base images, and keep ubuntu20.04 / glibc 2.31 for cu12 images or use musl static shim for edge cases.

jon: short-term mitigation: rollback the images that were pushed to eu-west and drain/reprovision the NotReady nodes. I can trigger rollback if SRE approves. @deploy-bot can we do a controlled rollback?

deploy-bot: scheduled rollback job rbk-1952345678 to eu-west pool. Draining 14 nodes, replacing with cu11 images. ETA ~18m. :white_check_mark:

mira: action items for runtime team: 1) split images by distro/toolkit, 2) run ldd/ldd-static checks as part of CI, 3) run small-scale canary with ubuntu18->20 variants before mass push.

lee: ops note — some nodes had old driver packages on host while container expected newer kernel modules. That produced OOMs in the plugin loader and made autoscaler mark hosts as unhealthy. Need host-driver audit next.

alex: for debugging, here's the ldd output from failing container: 
```
ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so
	linux-vdso.so.1 =>  (0x00007ffd...) 
	libm.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6 (0x00007f...) 
	libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x00007f...) # version 2.27
	/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (0x000056...)
```

mira: confirms glibc mismatch. longer term we should bake minimal glibc-compatible toolkits (or rely on distro packages) so we don't pull newer symbols into container userland.

kate: finance flagged the extra GPU-hours spend. we should run a cost/benefit before full cu12 roll: estimate dev productivity gains vs rebuild + vetting cost.

jon: also saw kubelet logs showing: `failed to map device plugin: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = could not load module 'nvidia_uvm'` on a subset of nodes — inconsistent host kernel module versions.

lee: plan: 1) rollback (in progress), 2) host-driver audit + mandatory kernel-driver alignment before any toolkit upgrades, 3) CI image policy for distro compatibility, 4) cost-impact report for exec.

mira: will add CI checks: run `strings libc.so.6 | grep GLIBC_` and fail if image contains symbols > distro baseline; run small canary in single AZ with 10% traffic.

alex: thanks. keeping this thread for RCA notes. once rollback completes I'll post node statuses and a short timeline. :thumbsup:
